narrative:
FY2026 budget revenue is USD 492.2B, +2.5% on FY2025 actuals of USD 480.0B. The Q3 forecast stands at USD 472.9B — USD 19.3B below budget, almost entirely on price: Brent has averaged USD 72/bbl against the USD 75 budget deck and the Asia OSP premium narrowed.

Onshore Crude Fields remain the engine at USD 118.3B (24% of group). Non-Associated Gas Fields are the fastest-growing asset (+5.5%) as Al-Rimal phase 2 came online three weeks early. Downstream revenue follows product prices: Ras Meridian Refining Complex USD 112.5B and International Refining JVs USD 91.7B.

Key risk: the offshore turnaround ran 11 days long, holding offshore volume 3% below plan this month.

signals.title: Brent sensitivity: $2.1B revenue per $1/bbl
signals.source: Meridian Corporate Planning — price deck model
signals.excerpt: Every $1/bbl Brent move changes FY2026 revenue by about $2.1B and net income by about $0.9B after the price-linked royalty tier and 46% effective tax.

signals.title: Q3 forecast $19B below the $492B budget
signals.excerpt: Lower realized prices across the chain drive the gap: crude fields −$8.3B, refining −$7.2B, gas −$1.2B and trading −$2.7B; volumes are broadly on plan.

signals.title: Gas expansion is the growth engine
signals.source: Meridian Gas Co. — Al-Rimal program review
signals.excerpt: Non-Associated Gas Fields revenue is budgeted 3 points above group growth as the Al-Rimal unconventional program ramps and frees crude for export.
